title: Audio content
description: The `audio` content block, carrying base64-encoded audio data and its MIME type.
question: Does an audio result survive adaptation?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: Audio is the least-implemented content type in the union, which makes it the sharpest test of whether a framework handles the content list generically or only the cases it happened to code for.

notes.crewai: CrewAI 1.15.26: returned on its own, the audio comes back as the stringified content model with its base64 data and `audio/wav` MIME type as characters. Beside other content kinds it is dropped and only the text reaches the agent.
notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `processResult` returns `{ error }` for `isError`, `structuredContent` when the server sent one, the joined text (JSON-parsed when it looks like JSON) when every block is text, the lone block when there is one, and otherwise the whole `CallToolResult`. A lone audio block is returned as the block itself, so it survives; in `mixed_content` the server also sent `structuredContent`, which is returned alone, and the audio is gone. With `createMcpHost({ multipart: true })`, a non-default option, audio becomes a `media` part beside the output.
notes.langchain: LangChain: `_convert_mcp_content_to_lc_block` raises NotImplementedError -- 'AudioContent conversion to LangChain content blocks is not yet supported' -- while building the result, so the whole call aborts and no part of it reaches the agent. Re-measured at both of LangChain's result boundaries and identical at each: the exception is not a `ToolException`, so the tool's `handle_tool_error` callback never sees it and the `ToolCall` invocation an agent makes raises exactly as the direct one does.
notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents: the block is serialized into a text block containing its JSON, base64 payload and all, so the audio reaches the agent only as characters.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: a result without `structuredContent` comes back unchanged, audio block intact with its data and mimeType. When the result carries `structuredContent`, that value is returned in place of the whole result and the audio is gone.
notes.google_adk: Google ADK 2.11.0: the tool's return value (`after_tool_callback`) is the dumped `CallToolResult`, with this block intact in `content`. The model receives that dict as `FunctionResponse.response`, a JSON value: the block survives as JSON text, and no media is lifted into `FunctionResponse.parts`.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): execute resolves with the CallToolResult, so a caller reading a step's toolResults gets the audio block intact. The adapter's toModelOutput converter maps only text and image blocks, so the model receives an audio block as a text part holding the block's JSON (type, MIME type and base64 data as characters). Boundary-dependent: kept at execute, flattened to text at model_output.
notes.ms_agent_framework: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: a lone audio block becomes a `data` `Content` with a data URI and media type. Beside `structuredContent` it is dropped, because the default `tool_result_content="structured_first"` hands the model only the structured JSON.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: Boundary-dependent. `McpWorkbench.call_tool` raises `Unknown content type from server` on an `AudioContent` block and returns the message as an error result, which the agent also receives; `mcp_server_tools`' `run_json` returns the `AudioContent` block.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `map_mcp_content_to_tool_result_content` has no audio branch, so an audio block is dropped with a debug log, alone or beside other blocks.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the model receives an audio block as its JSON serialization inside a text item (`{"type":"audio",...}`); `MCPServer.callTool` itself returns the block intact.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: boundary-dependent. `Kernel.invoke` returns AudioContent. The model's tool message is the Python repr of that object; no audio part is sent.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `FunctionTool._parse_tool_output` has no case for `CallToolResult`, so the `ToolOutput`, and the `ChatMessage(role="tool")` a `FunctionAgent` sends the model, hold one text block: the result's Python repr. The audio survives only as characters inside that repr; the model gets no audio part.
notes.pi: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient.callTool` keeps the audio block. `toLlmContent` replaces it with the text `[audio <mimeType> omitted]`, so no audio reaches the model.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: boundary-dependent. `MCPTool.runAsync` returns the `CallToolResult` unchanged (`afterToolCallback` sees it with every block intact), and ADK puts that object in the `functionResponse` of the next `LlmRequest`. At `direct` the audio block keeps its data and mimeType. At `agent` it is a JSON value inside `functionResponse.response`; no audio part is sent.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): boundary-dependent. The direct `Tool.invoke` return is that JSON string, which the adapter's docstring says to read with `json.loads`; parsed, it keeps every block. The `ChatMessage` an `Agent` hands the next generator turn carries the Tool's return value as one text: the `CallToolResult` JSON from `model_dump_json`. The audio arrives as base64 inside that text, not as an audio block.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `MCPAdaptTool.forward` decodes audio only with `torchaudio`, which `smolagents[mcp]` does not install, so an audio result raises `ValueError: Audio content requires the torchaudio package` and a `ToolCallingAgent` sends the model an `Error:` message. Beside other content kinds it is dropped, because `MCPAdaptTool.forward` reads only `content[0]` and logs a warning when there are more.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: with the default `result_mode="text"`, `Tool.acall` returns the audio block as the MCP content object when the result has no text (direct: `y`). In a `dspy.ReAct` run the observation the model reads is that object's Python repr, `«type='audio' data='...' mime_type='audio/wav' ...»` (react: `a`). When a result carries any text block, `_convert_mcp_tool_result` returns the text alone and drops the audio block at both boundaries.
notes.spring_ai: Spring AI 2.0.1: the tool result reaches the agent and a direct `ToolCallback.call` as one string: the JSON of the result's content list with each block's `type` field dropped, e.g. `[{"data":"UklGR...","mimeType":"audio/wav"}]`. The base64 survives as characters in a string, with nothing marking it as audio.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `MCPTool.run` returns the `AudioContent` object (direct: `y`), but drops it next to `structuredContent`. The model gets it as one JSON string with the base64 data inline, not as audio (agent: `a`).
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): depends on the boundary. `agent`: the `tool` message the provider receives is an empty string, and unlike an image the audio is not forwarded in a follow-up message. `direct`: `session.rpc.tools.execute` returns the `audio` block whole.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient._call_tool_impl` keeps only `content[0]`, returning its `text` when it has one and `str(content[0])` otherwise. Returned on its own, the audio comes back as the stringified content model ({shape}), so {kept} survive only as characters, at `BaseTool.run` and in the tool message the agent loop builds. Beside other content kinds it is dropped and only the leading text reaches the agent.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `AbstractMcpTool.wrapCallResult` turns a result that holds any block other than text into `{"error": "Tool '<name>' returned content that is not TextContent.", "content_details": ...}` when no text block is present, and drops the non-text blocks when one is (`mixed_content` returns only the text). Both boundaries see the same map.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: The default `McpToolExecutor` result converter accepts text blocks only. Any `audio` block makes it throw `Unsupported content type: "audio"`: the direct executor raises it as a `RuntimeException`, and AiServices turns it into an error tool result the model reads in place of the block. A result with `structuredContent` never reads its blocks at all.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: boundary-dependent. At `direct` the audio block keeps its data and mimeType. `AIAgent` sends the tool's result to the model as one `role: tool` message whose content is `McpTool.encodeResultToString`: the JSON of the whole `CallToolResult` (`content`, `isError`, `structuredContent`), or `Error: <text>` when `isError` is set. At `agent` the base64 data is a string inside that JSON; no audio part reaches the model.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcpTool.Run` returns `{"output": text}`, where `formatMCPContent` replaces the block with a placeholder line (`[MCP audio: mimeType="audio/wav", size=44 bytes]`, with no audio data), and the model receives that map as `FunctionResponse.response`. When the result also has `structuredContent`, as in the mixed result, `Run` returns `{"output": structuredContent}` and the block is dropped.
notes.ms_agent_framework_dotnet: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): a lone audio block becomes a `DataContent` with its bytes and MIME type at both boundaries. Beside `structuredContent` (`mixed_content`) `McpClientTool` returns the `CallToolResult` as JSON, so the audio reaches the model as base64 characters inside a text result, not as audio.

verdict.detail: An unsupported content type that raises rather than degrades turns a partially supported result into a failed call.

summary: An adapter that raises on a block it cannot convert, instead of degrading it, loses the rest of the result with it.
